input_messages.content: Hello, I’m having some trouble with my phone. I’ve been trying to send a picture message—what I think you call an MMS?—to my daughter, but it just won’t go through. This has been happening for a few hours now. Can you help me fix it?
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that’s enough—do you need anything else from me?
I just checked my phone, and I see a little airplane icon at the top. Does that mean something is wrong? I’m not sure about the other things you asked—should I try making a call or sending a text?
Okay, I turned off Airplane Mode like you said. Now I see something that says "No Signal" and "Data Disabled" at the top of my screen. What should I do next?
I checked, and it looks like my phone says there’s no SIM card detected. What does that mean? Is that bad?
Alright, I took out the SIM card and put it back in. Now I see a little signal bar at the top, but it says "2G" and "Data Disabled." Is that better? What should I do next?

I went ahead and changed the network mode to prefer 4G or 5G, and I also turned on mobile data. Now I see "5G" and "Data Enabled" at the top of my screen. Should I try sending the picture message again now?
I just tried, but it still won’t let me send the picture message. It’s still not working—what should I do now?

I checked my phone’s APN settings, and I see the APN name is “internet” and there’s an MMSC URL listed as “http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc.” Does that look right, or do I need to change something? I’m not really sure what any of this means.
I restarted my phone like you said, but I still can’t send picture messages. This is getting a bit frustrating—why isn’t it working? What else can we try?

I checked, and it looks like Wi-Fi Calling is turned on right now. Should I go ahead and turn it off, or do you want me to check the app permissions first? I just want to make sure I’m doing the right thing.
I turned off Wi-Fi Calling and tried sending the picture message again, but it still won’t go through. What should I do next?
I checked my messaging app’s permissions, and it looks like it has permission for SMS and phone, but I don’t see anything about storage. Is that a problem? How do I give it permission for storage?

I gave the messaging app permission to access storage, but I still can’t send picture messages. Is there anything else we can try? I’m starting to get a bit worried—will I ever be able to send photos again?

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

messages.content: Hi! How can I help you today?

Hello, I’m having some trouble with my phone. I’ve been trying to send a picture message—what I think you call an MMS?—to my daughter, but it just won’t go through. This has been happening for a few hours now. Can you help me fix it?

Thank you for reaching out about your MMS issue. I can help you troubleshoot this problem.

To get started, I’ll need to identify your account. Could you please provide one of the following:
- The phone number associated with your account,
- Your full name and date of birth (in YYYY-MM-DD format), or
- Your customer ID (if you have it)?

Once I have this information, I can assist you further.
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that’s enough—do you need anything else from me?

{"customer_id": "C1001", "full_name": "John Smith", "date_of_birth": "1985-06-15", "email": "john.smith@example.com", "phone_number": "555-123-2002", "address": {"street": "123 Main St", "city": "Anytown", "state": "CA", "zip_code": "90210"}, "account_status": "Active", "payment_methods": [{"method_type": "Credit Card", "account_number_last_4": "1235", "expiration_date": "12/2026"}], "line_ids": ["L1001", "L1002", "L1003"], "bill_ids": ["B1001", "B1002", "B1003"], "created_at": "2025-01-15 10:30:00", "last_extension_date": null, "goodwill_credit_used_this_year": 25.0}

Thank you for providing your information. I have identified your account.

To help you send picture messages (MMS), I’ll need to check a few things about your phone and service. Could you please let me know:
- Are you able to make regular calls and send text messages?
- Are you currently connected to mobile data (not just Wi-Fi)?
- Are you seeing any error messages when you try to send the MMS?

Your answers will help me guide you through the right troubleshooting steps.
Status Bar: ✈️ Airplane Mode | 🔋 80%
I just checked my phone, and I see a little airplane icon at the top. Does that mean something is wrong? I’m not sure about the other things you asked—should I try making a call or sending a text?

The airplane icon means that Airplane Mode is enabled on your phone. When Airplane Mode is on, all wireless connections—including cellular service, mobile data, and Wi-Fi—are turned off. This will prevent you from sending MMS, making calls, or sending texts.

Please turn off Airplane Mode on your phone. You can usually do this by:
1. Swiping down from the top of your screen to open the quick settings menu.
2. Tapping the airplane icon to disable Airplane Mode.

Once you’ve turned it off, check if you can make a call or send a text. Then, try sending your picture message again. Let me know if this resolves the issue or if you need further assistance.

Airplane Mode is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📵 No Signal | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%
Okay, I turned off Airplane Mode like you said. Now I see something that says "No Signal" and "Data Disabled" at the top of my screen. What should I do next?

Thank you for the update. Seeing "No Signal" and "Data Disabled" means your phone is not currently connected to the cellular network or mobile data, which is required for sending MMS.

Let’s troubleshoot step by step:

1. First, let’s check your SIM card status to make sure it’s recognized by your phone.
2. Then, we’ll check your mobile data settings.

I’ll guide you through the process. Could you please check your SIM card status on your phone? If you’re not sure how, let me know and I can provide instructions.
No SIM card detected in the phone.
I checked, and it looks like my phone says there’s no SIM card detected. What does that mean? Is that bad?

If your phone says there’s no SIM card detected, it means your phone cannot connect to the cellular network, which is necessary for calls, texts, and MMS. This is likely the reason you’re unable to send picture messages.

Let’s try a simple fix:
Please remove your SIM card from your phone and then reinsert it. This is called “reseating” the SIM card and can often resolve detection issues.

After you’ve done this, check if your phone now recognizes the SIM card and if you see signal bars at the top of your screen. Let me know what you see after reseating the SIM card.

SIM card re-seated successfully.
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%
Alright, I took out the SIM card and put it back in. Now I see a little signal bar at the top, but it says "2G" and "Data Disabled." Is that better? What should I do next?

That’s progress! Your phone now detects the SIM card and has some signal, but it’s connected to a 2G network and mobile data is still disabled. MMS usually requires at least a 3G connection and mobile data to be enabled.

Let’s do the following steps:
1. Change your network mode to prefer 4G or 5G, if available.
2. Enable mobile data.

Would you like instructions on how to change your network mode and enable mobile data, or do you know how to do this on your device?

Preferred Network Mode set to: 4g_5g_preferred
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%

Mobile Data is now ON.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

I went ahead and changed the network mode to prefer 4G or 5G, and I also turned on mobile data. Now I see "5G" and "Data Enabled" at the top of my screen. Should I try sending the picture message again now?

Yes, now that your phone shows "5G" and "Data Enabled," your device is connected to a high-speed network with mobile data active. Please try sending your picture message (MMS) again.

Let me know if it goes through successfully or if you encounter any issues. If it still doesn’t work, I’ll guide you through the next troubleshooting steps.
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
I just tried, but it still won’t let me send the picture message. It’s still not working—what should I do now?

Thank you for letting me know. Since you now have signal and mobile data enabled but still can’t send MMS, the next step is to check your phone’s APN (Access Point Name) settings. Incorrect APN settings are a common cause of MMS issues.

Could you please check your APN settings and let me know if you see an MMSC (Multimedia Messaging Service Center) URL listed? If you’re not sure how to check, I can provide instructions.

Current APN Name: internet
MMSC URL (for picture messages): http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)

I checked my phone’s APN settings, and I see the APN name is “internet” and there’s an MMSC URL listed as “http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc.” Does that look right, or do I need to change something? I’m not really sure what any of this means.

Thank you for checking your APN settings and providing the details. The APN name and MMSC URL you listed appear to be in the correct format, so your APN settings are likely not the issue.

Let’s try a couple more troubleshooting steps:
1. Restart your phone. This can help apply any recent changes and refresh your network connection.
2. After restarting, try sending the picture message again.

If it still doesn’t work after the restart, please let me know. We can then check for other possible causes, such as messaging app permissions or Wi-Fi Calling settings.

Restarting network services...
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
I restarted my phone like you said, but I still can’t send picture messages. This is getting a bit frustrating—why isn’t it working? What else can we try?

Thank you for your patience. Since restarting didn’t resolve the issue, let’s check a few more things that can affect MMS:

1. Is Wi-Fi Calling enabled on your phone? Sometimes, having Wi-Fi Calling ON can interfere with MMS. If it’s ON, please try turning it OFF and then send the picture message again.
2. Does your messaging app have permission to access storage and SMS? The app needs these permissions to send MMS. If you’re not sure, I can guide you on how to check and enable these permissions.

Could you please check if Wi-Fi Calling is enabled and let me know? If you need instructions, just ask.
Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned ON.

I checked, and it looks like Wi-Fi Calling is turned on right now. Should I go ahead and turn it off, or do you want me to check the app permissions first? I just want to make sure I’m doing the right thing.

Please go ahead and turn off Wi-Fi Calling first. After you turn it off, try sending the picture message again.

If it still doesn’t work, we’ll then check your messaging app’s permissions together.

Let me know what happens after you turn off Wi-Fi Calling and try to send the MMS.

Wi-Fi Calling is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
I turned off Wi-Fi Calling and tried sending the picture message again, but it still won’t go through. What should I do next?

Thank you for trying that. The next step is to check your messaging app’s permissions. The app needs permission to access storage (for pictures) and SMS (for sending messages).

Please check your messaging app’s permissions and make sure both “storage” and “SMS” permissions are enabled. If you’re not sure how to do this, let me know your phone’s make and model, and I can provide step-by-step instructions. Once you’ve checked or updated the permissions, try sending the picture message again and let me know the result.
The following apps are installed on the phone: messaging, browser
App 'messaging' has permission for: sms, phone.
I checked my messaging app’s permissions, and it looks like it has permission for SMS and phone, but I don’t see anything about storage. Is that a problem? How do I give it permission for storage?

Yes, not having storage permission can prevent your messaging app from sending picture messages (MMS), since it needs access to your photos.

To fix this, you’ll need to grant storage permission to your messaging app. Here’s how you can do it on most Android phones:

1. Open your phone’s Settings app.
2. Tap on “Apps” or “Applications.”
3. Find and select your messaging app from the list.
4. Tap on “Permissions.”
5. Look for “Storage” and enable it (toggle it ON or select “Allow”).

If you’re using an iPhone, the steps are:
1. Open the Settings app.
2. Scroll down and tap on your messaging app (usually “Messages”).
3. Make sure “Photos” is set to “Read and Write.”

After granting storage permission, try sending the picture message again. Let me know if this resolves the issue or if you need more help.

Success. Permission 'storage' granted to app 'messaging'.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.

I gave the messaging app permission to access storage, but I still can’t send picture messages. Is there anything else we can try? I’m starting to get a bit worried—will I ever be able to send photos again?

Thank you for your patience and for following all the troubleshooting steps so far. I understand this is frustrating, and I want to make sure we resolve this for you.

We’ve checked:
- Airplane mode (now off)
- SIM card (now detected)
- Network mode (now 5G)
- Mobile data (enabled)
- APN/MMSC settings (appear correct)
- Device restart (done)
- Wi-Fi Calling (now off)
- Messaging app permissions (now granted)

Since you’re still unable to send MMS after all these steps, this may indicate a deeper technical issue with your line or account that requires specialized support.

I will transfer you to a human agent who can investigate further and ensure your MMS service is restored.
